column1: # LeekWallet Partition Table - SECURE TARGET (16MB Flash)
# Offsets differ from partitions.csv for two compounding reasons
# silent bricks if they are got wrong.
# 1. A signed bootloader is 0xB000 (0xA000 of code padded to a sector boundary
#    plus a 0x1000 signature sector) and so pushes the partition table from the
#    default 0x8000 out to 0xF000.
# 2. Secure boot v2 signs the partition table too

column2: not the usual 0x1000: partitions-signed.bin is 8192 bytes. With

column1: #    the table at 0xF000 it spans 0xF000-0x11000
#    offset of 0x10000 sat UNDER the table's own signature sector. Flashing
#    that image writes the signature over the first 4 KB of the vault - and it
#    boots anyway
column2: because a freshly formatted NVS has nothing there to lose.

column1: #    It would have started eating wallet data on a provisioned board. Caught by
#    scripts/preflight-secure.sh
# nvs therefore starts at 0x12000
column2: leaving a 4 KB margin below it. The app

column1: # stays at 0x20000 because app partitions must be 64 KB aligned.
